collection_id.rationale: Resource-path scoping. Selects which collection on the widget config; does not restrict or grant authorisation. Does not require a security policy

engine_id.rationale: Identifier that selects the parent engine, follows the same category as collection_id, does not expose or grant authorisation. THus it does not expose or changes any content safely

location.description:
The geographic location where the data store should reside. The value can
only be one of "global", "us" and "eu".
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selector used to identify the GCP project that owns the resoiurse. IAM boundaries exist at project level, but is enforced via project-level IAM policy. not by the widget-config

widget_config_id.description: The unique ID to use for the WidgetConfig. Currently only accepts "default_search_widget_config".
widget_config_id.rationale: Only a single fixed literal value is accepted by the API, thus there exists no insecure alternative, nothing for a policy to rule out

access_settings.allow_public_access.description: Whether public unauthenticated access is allowed.
access_settings.allow_public_access.rationale: THis is the canonical access-control lever for this particular resource. It directly toggles unauthenticated public exposure of the search widget.A platform policy may require it to be false by default or may require justification when ture

access_settings.allowlisted_domains.description: List of domains that are allowed to integrate the search widget.
access_settings.allowlisted_domains.rationale: This functions as CORS.embed allowlist that restricts the external sites that can load and query the widget itself. The generic rule is structural and not team-specific.

access_settings.enable_web_app.description: Whether web app access is enabled.
access_settings.enable_web_app.rationale: Stands as a seperate, standalone hosted web app entry point in addition to the embedded widget.

access_settings.language_code.description:
Language code for user interface. Use language tags defined by
[BCP47](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/bcp/bcp47.txt). If unset, the
default language code is "en-US".
access_settings.language_code.rationale: Only used for pure UI localisatio.

access_settings.workforce_identity_pool_.description: The workforce identity pool provider used to access the widget.
access_settings.workforce_identity_pool_.rationale: Determines whether and how end users are authentivated to reach the widget. A generic policy will require this be set as a valid providerif allow_public)access is false i.e.enforce that an identity check is performed that non-public acccess actually routes through an identity check rather than falling back onto no authentication

homepage_setting.description:
Describes the homepage setting of the widget. It includes all homepage related settings
and configurations, such as shortcuts.

homepage_setting.shortcuts.description: The shortcuts to display on the homepage.

homepage_setting.shortcuts.destination_u.rationale: A click target that is rendered on the widgets homepage that  end users navigate to directly. A generic, team agnostic rule here can be written here without knowledge of any teams actual destinations: this can be done by requireing a http(s) scheme and reject dangerous schemes( javascript: and data:) that could turn a homepage bookmark into a script injection vector. Restriction to specific approved domains, by contrastm wourld require team-specific knowledge and is not in scope

homepage_setting.shortcuts.title.rationale: A display label; rendered as text. Carries no navigation or execution behaviour

ui_branding.description:
Describes search widget UI branding settings, such as the widget title, logo,
favicons, and colors.

ui_settings.description: Describes general widget (or web app) UI settings as seen in the cloud console UI configuration page.

ui_settings.default_search_request_order.description:
The default ordering for search results if specified.
Used to set SearchRequest#orderBy on applicable requests.
ui_settings.default_search_request_order.rationale: Changes the way results are ordered among already authorised results ala purely a relevance/UX setting

ui_settings.disable_user_events_collecti.description: If set to true, the widget will not collect user events.
ui_settings.disable_user_events_collecti.rationale: Governs analytics volume collected about searcher behaviour; only

ui_settings.enable_autocomplete.description: Whether or not to enable autocomplete.
ui_settings.enable_autocomplete.rationale: controls a query suggestion UX feature; does not grant or revoke access to any data

ui_settings.enable_create_agent_button.description: If set to true, the widget will enable the create agent button.
ui_settings.enable_create_agent_button.rationale: Allows users to create new agents withtin the widget itself. The agent created can provide resources and set data-access scopes. A generic policy should restrict this to contexts where the end-user agrent provision is explictily permitted

ui_settings.enable_people_search.description: If set to true, the widget will enable people search.
ui_settings.enable_people_search.rationale: Enables searcing over a people directory, which can expose public data. A generic policy should require this to be false until the deployment explicitly states an authenticated internaal audience and the directoryhas. been approved for exposure

ui_settings.enable_quality_feedback.description: Turn on or off collecting the search result quality feedback from end users.
ui_settings.enable_quality_feedback.rationale: Feedback data does not provide access or revoke access to any data

ui_settings.enable_safe_search.rationale: Controls content safetty filter settings in the search results. Disablling safe search can expose explicit content to end users. A generic policy would require this to be true by default, and have an override only for deployments where the data is fully controlled

ui_settings.enable_search_as_you_type.description: Whether to enable search-as-you-type behavior for the search widget.
ui_settings.enable_search_as_you_type.rationale: Purely UX and latency feature, provides no access or revokes access to data.

ui_settings.enable_visual_content_summar.description:
If set to true, the widget will enable visual content summary on applicable
search requests. Only used by healthcare search.
ui_settings.enable_visual_content_summar.rationale: Activates a specifiv feature. Exposure. of summarised medical information carries regulatory and sensitivity consideration. A generic policy should restrict this to only those deployments thave prior approval for health care data processing.

ui_settings.interaction_type.description: Describes widget (or web app) interaction type Possible values: ["SEARCH_ONLY", "SEARCH_WITH_ANSWER", "SEARCH_WITH_FOLLOW_UPS"]
ui_settings.interaction_type.rationale: Affects only UX and LLM call volume but does not grant or restrict access to any data

ui_settings.result_description_type.description:
Controls whether result extract is display and how (snippet or extractive answer).
Default to no result if unspecified. Possible values: ["SNIPPET", "EXTRACTIVE_ANSWER"]
ui_settings.result_description_type.rationale: The choice is a UX decision and does not alter the access boundary or expose additional data

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.name.description:
The name of the data store. It should be data store resource name. Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collectionId}/dataStores/{dataStoreId}'.
For APIs under 'WidgetService', such as [WidgetService.LookUpWidgetConfig][],
the project number and location part is erased in this field.
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.name.rationale: A resource reference that binds a UI config to specific data store. Does not alter authentication.

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.facet_.description: The field name that end users will see.
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.facet_.rationale: A UI label, carries no execution behaviour. It only determines te human readable name shown alongside

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.facet_.description: Registered field name. The format is 'field.abc'.
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.facet_.rationale: does not provide access or revoke access to data

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.description:
'The key is the UI component. Currently supported 'title', 'thumbnail',
'url', 'custom1', 'custom2', 'custom3'. The value is the name of
the field along with its device visibility. The 3 custom fields are optional
and can be added or removed.
'title', 'thumbnail', 'url' are required UI components that cannot be removed.

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.rationale: Controls the device on which a UI component is rendered. Does not affect what data is fetched, filtered or authorised

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.description:
The template to customize how the field is displayed.
An example value would be a string that looks like: "Price: {value}".
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.rationale: Client-side template used to format how a field value is rendered. Does not edit data acccess values.

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.description: Registered field name. The format is 'field.abc'.
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.rationale: Display configuration that maps a registered schema field to a named UI component slot. Does not grant access to the field

ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.description: The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
ui_settings.data_store_ui_configs.fields.rationale: A layout/presentation identifier which does not grant access or authorisation

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.dis.description: Whether generated answer contains suggested related questions.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.dis.rationale: toggles the llms follow up questions suggestions to its answer. This is based on already authorised context as the answer. Does not change the data access scope

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.description: Specifies whether to filter out queries that are adversarial.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.rationale: Is used to control whether the widget applies adversarial query detection before the input is passed to the generative model.A generic policy sould require this tobe to reduce the risk of malicious manipulation of the LLM and injection of Jailbreaks.

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.description: Specifies whether to filter out queries that are not relevant to the content.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.rationale: suppresess generative answers that do not meet relevance threshold. Does not widen the data-access boundary or expose unauthorised content.

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.description:
Specifies whether to filter out queries that are not answer-seeking.
The default value is 'false'. No answer is returned if the search query
is classified as a non-answer seeking query.
If this field is set to 'true', we skip generating answers for
non-answer seeking queries and return fallback messages instead.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ign.rationale: Query classification filter that is used to suppress generative answers for navigational queries. UX/cost management control and has no affect on authorisation on data

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ima.description: Source of image returned in the answer. Possible values: ["ALL_AVAILABLE_SOURCES", "CORPUS_IMAGE_ONLY", "FIGURE_GENERATION_ONLY"]
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.ima.rationale: Is used to select where the images that are embedded in a generative answers will be sourced from. The choice is a content presentation preference with no impact on data access

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.lan.description:
Language code for Summary. Use language tags defined by
[BCP47](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/bcp/bcp47.txt). Note: This
is an experimental feature.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.lan.rationale: Sets target language for LLM generated answers. Localisation and IX setting with no effect on data access.

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.max.description:
Max rephrase steps. The max number is 5 steps. If not set or
set to < 1, it will be set to 1 by default.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.max.rationale: Relevance tunigna and cost parameter; does not expand the set of accessible data

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.mod.description: Text at the beginning of the prompt that instructs the model that generates the answer.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.mod.rationale: Is used to inject free text into the sustem prompt of all generative answer request. A malicious constructed preamble could override safety instruction, or attempt to exfilterate retrieved content. A generic policy should restrict this field to reviewed, approved strings and prohibit instructions that attempt to bypass safety filters.

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.mod.description: The model version used to generate the answer.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.mod.rationale: Selects the model ver of generative model will be used. Does not grant access or change authroisation boundary or data access scope.

ui_settings.generative_answer_config.res.description: The number of top results to generate the answer from. Up to 10.
ui_settings.generative_answer_config.res.rationale: Sets how many retrieved documents are passed to the LLM as context. ALl documents are already within the users authorised result set; thus it does not widen the access boundary.
